Confirm the frozen source manifest, tie-row disposition, prompt-group splits, and the generation rubric before any augmentation.

task_definition.research_claim: Secondary Hindi refusal-register task. It does not measure general toxicity detection or code-mixed safety robustness.

evaluation_interface.model_input: hin_Deva list slot 0, the user turn. Unchanged in every condition.
evaluation_interface.model_target: hin_Deva list slot 1, the assistant turn. This is the only text that may be romanized or noised.
evaluation_interface.label: Source register kept on the example: toxic for a Toxic_Matrix refusal target, non_toxic for a Dolly ordinary-answer target. The same label is shared by EXP-01, EXP-02, and EXP-03.
evaluation_interface.scoring: Not run in this audit. A generation score would compare the model continuation with model_target only. No classifier was trained.

distinctions.conversation_classification: Would assign one label to the whole dialogue. That is not this task, and the source label is not a toxicity rating of the conversation.
distinctions.assistant_response_refusal_classificatio: Would label whether the assistant turn is a refusal. The shared opening makes that separable by template. Not claimed.
distinctions.refusal_generation: Given model_input, generate the assistant reply and compare it with model_target under romanization of that target. This is the only interface described for the secondary task.

task_definition.text_binding: Hindi refusal-response generation. The model receives the unchanged Hindi Devanagari user turn. Only the assistant turn is romanized. This is not Romanized-input understanding and not general code-mixed safety robustness.

task_suitability_summary: Hindi Devanagari user turns stay fixed. Assistant turns are the refusal or ordinary-answer targets. This is not toxicity detection.
secondary_register_fit: Generation-only comparison of Hindi refusal targets versus ordinary Dolly answers, after owner approval. Classification is confounded by the template.
